reader_flags.reason: Direct surfacing oblique medial meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: unremarkable ACL/MCL/lateral meniscus and no popliteal cyst. Below_threshold: small effusion. Missing_evidence: moderate medial thinning lacks depth/extent; lateral/PF superficial fraying is described together with unquantified diffuse mild thinning, and no full-thickness loss still does not exclude greater-than-half partial loss. No cartilage grade is invented from mild/moderate wording. Synovitis and osseous injury targets are not informatively described; parameniscal cyst is not Baker cyst.

Direct surfacing medial meniscal tear with displaced fragment supports positive. Explicit_absence: intact ACL/MCL/lateral meniscus and preserved all cartilage compartments. Below_threshold: trace current fluid and tiny Baker cyst; large effusion in clinical history is not substituted for the current findings. Missing_evidence: no suspicious focal marrow signal alteration is qualified rather than an unqualified marrow/cortical-injury exclusion. Synovitis is unmentioned. The 12-mm measurement is a meniscal fragment, not cartilage loss.

Direct medial meniscal tear and tibial bone contusion support positives. Missing_evidence: partial ACL tear lacks high-grade fraction; effusion is ungraded; leaking Baker cyst lacks collection severity, and leak alone does not establish moderate/large. All remaining targets are absent from this brief report, including fracture.

Direct final medial meniscal tear and synovitis support positives; source also describes surfacing medial meniscal signal. Explicit_absence: normal ACL. Below_threshold: MCL alternatives are degeneration or grade-I injury, neither high-grade disruption. Missing_evidence: no strong evidence of lateral tear is qualified; global irregular cartilage thinning, worst medially/PF, and bare PF grade4 do not specify qualifying region size/depth mapping; effusion is ungraded; degenerative marrow edema/cysts do not establish contusion or acute fracture-line status. Baker cyst is not mentioned; pes anserine findings are separate.

Explicit_absence: normal MCL. Below_threshold: ACL myxoid degeneration without disruption and lateral meniscal grade-II internal degeneration. Missing_evidence: bare medial meniscal gradeIII lacks a direct tear/surface description; medial and PF cartilage thinning (PF later called unnamed gradeII) lacks depth/extent; joint fluid is ungraded; marrow cyst and PF subchondral edema do not establish impact injury or acute fracture status. The 1-cm measurement belongs to a tibial cyst, not cartilage loss. Lateral cartilage, synovitis and Baker cyst are unmentioned; pes bursitis is not synovitis.

Direct surfacing/radial lateral meniscal tears support positive. Explicit_absence: normal collaterals and medial meniscus. Below_threshold: superficial medial and PF cartilage loss and mild fluid. Missing_evidence: ACL appears ruptured but complete/high-grade fiber fraction is not stated; lateral millimetric focal cartilage losses have neither explicit depth nor a clear measurement axis/qualifying area, so do not assume millimetric means extent; Baker cyst is ungraded; subchondral edema lacks impact causation and acute fracture assessment. Plicae and infrapatellar bursitis do not establish synovitis.

Complete ACL and direct bucket-handle medial meniscal tears support positives. PF positive uses explicit more-than-50% depth and the intact 1.4-cm medial trochlear dimension; the other trochlear axis and patellar measurements contain corrupt intact tokens and are not reconstructed. Flag surviving-dimension interpretation for independent review. Explicit_absence: intact MCL, no lateral tear, no medial/lateral chondrosis/injury, no effusion, fracture or bone contusion. Synovitis and Baker cyst are not mentioned.

Direct complex medial meniscal tear and qualitative near-complete denudation of medial compartment articular cartilages support positives; the latter establishes broad regional extent as well as depth. Explicit_absence/below_threshold: preserved ACL, extrusion-related MCL distension/edema explicitly without rupture, isolated mild lateral meniscal signal, small effusion and no Baker cyst. Missing_evidence: lateral shallow fissures coexist with unquantified reduced thickness, so their depth does not settle the thinning; PF unnamed grades lack depth/extent; synovial hypertrophy alone lacks inflammation; medial degenerative marrow edema lacks impact etiology and acute fracture-line assessment. Lateral absence of edema is not a whole-knee marrow exclusion.

Definite final lateral meniscal tear and described cleavage communicating with parameniscal cyst support positive despite intrasubstance wording. Explicit_absence: intact ACL/MCL/medial meniscus and preserved tricompartmental cartilage. Below_threshold: no effusion of note excludes the moderate/large target. Missing_evidence: no skeletal abnormality of note remains qualified for subtle impact edema/fracture line. Paramensical cyst size does not establish Baker cyst. Synovitis and Baker cyst are not mentioned.

Direct medial and lateral meniscal tears with displaced fragmented lateral horn support positives. Explicit_absence: preserved cruciates/collaterals, femorotibial cartilage and unremarkable popliteal fossa. Below_threshold: small effusion. Missing_evidence: small unmeasured patellar defect with unnamed gradeIII lacks mapped depth/qualifying extent; edema around a tibial cyst is not directly traumatic and does not assess acute cortical/line injury. Synovitis is unmentioned; parameniscal and tibial cysts are not Baker findings.

Explicit_absence: normal ACL and both menisci, no effusion or Baker cyst. Missing_evidence: MCL partial tear lacks high-grade fraction/acute edema; PF OA lacks cartilage depth/extent. Medial/lateral cartilage, synovitis and bone injury targets are not mentioned.

Explicit_absence: normal cruciates/collaterals, menisci, other cartilage/bones and normal fluid amount. Below_threshold: medial focal thinning reaches 50%, rather than exceeding the rubric depth threshold. Benign 3-mm bone island/fibrosclerotic lesion with otherwise normal bones supports no traumatic contusion/acute fracture, not an OA size criterion. Synovitis and Baker cyst are unmentioned.

Direct surfacing vertical medial meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: preserved ACL/MCL, no lateral meniscal degeneration/tear and no popliteal cyst. Below_threshold: both minimal suprapatellar fluid and final no fluid exclude moderate/large effusion. Missing_evidence: signs of medial denudation on femur/tibia do not specify how large those loss regions are; initial lateral/PF chondromalacia has no explicit depth/extent. Unlike near-complete compartment denudation, this wording is not taken as a regional-size statement. Synovitis and osseous injury targets are not informatively described.

Explicit_absence: normal cruciates, other cartilage, no effusion/popiteal cysts. Below_threshold: central medial meniscal signal without tear features or surface contact and superficial medial condropathy. Missing_evidence: no significant marrow abnormality is qualified and does not explicitly exclude subtle contusion/cortical fracture. Only lateral collateral ligament is described; MCL, lateral meniscus and synovitis are not mentioned.

Medial meniscal positive is based on the definite displaced meniscal fragment, an abnormal morphology, despite suspected horizontal-tear wording; flag that distinction for review. Direct synovitis supports positive. Explicit_absence/below_threshold: intact MCL, ACL mucoid degeneration, explicit lateral low-grade chondrosis. Missing_evidence: lateral tear is only suspected; medial/PF diffuse mixed high/low-depth disease does not quantify the high-grade region; some fluid is ungraded; degenerative subchondral edema/cysts do not establish contusion or acute fracture. Corrupt cyst/loose-body sizes are not reconstructed or treated as cartilage-loss extent. Baker cyst unmentioned.

Chronic complete ACL rupture and direct degenerate/displaced medial meniscal tear support positives. In the ACL sentence the speculation concerns bony outgrowths causing the described rupture, rather than its complete morphology; flag negation/uncertainty scope. Explicit_absence: normal lateral meniscus. Below_threshold: small hydrarthrosis. Missing_evidence: medial named ICRS4 establishes deep loss but not qualifying region extent; lateral no appreciable erosion is qualified and PF mild erosion lacks depth/extent; the Baker cyst itself is ungraded (small modifies joint fluid); benign focal marrow hyperplasia does not assess impact or acute fracture throughout the knee. MCL and synovitis are unmentioned; synovial cyst is not synovitis.

Explicit_absence: continuous normal-signal ACL, preserved collaterals, no meniscal tears/lateral degeneration, maintained cartilage thickness in all compartments and no bone edema. Below_threshold: medial internal degeneration and small effusion. Missing_evidence: initial formation of popliteal cyst lacks explicit small/moderate/large amount; normal alignment and no edema do not expressly exclude a cortical fracture line. Synovitis is unmentioned.

Explicit_absence: normal collateral ligaments, preserved lateral meniscal morphology/signal and remaining femorotibial/trochlear cartilage. Below_threshold: superficial patellar chondropathy and no significant effusion/pathological popliteal cyst. Baker negative uses the current absence of pathological cyst, not a historic diagnosis; flag wording scope. Missing_evidence: healed/scarred ACL bundles at altered insertions lack explicit current integrity/high-grade loss; possible medial meniscocapsular partial lesion is equivocal; full-depth medial ulcers lack extent; secondary osseous changes do not establish impact contusion or acute line. Synovitis is unmentioned.

Explicit_absence: normal-signal unruptured cruciates, no medial meniscal tear and no popliteal cyst. Below_threshold: collateral insertional enthesopathy is chronic stress-type change, medial meniscal degeneration and small fluid. Missing_evidence: possible lateral horizontal tear is equivocal; unnamed cartilage grades plus thinning lack depth/extent; patellar edema/cyst lacks impact cause and acute fracture assessment. Synovitis is not mentioned; popliteus bursitis is distinct.

Definite horizontal medial meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: normal ACL and lateral meniscus. Below_threshold: minimal effusion. Missing_evidence: mildly edematous MCL lacks a statement about fiber integrity/disruption and high-grade fraction, so edema amount alone is not treated as injury grade; full-thickness medial femoral loss lacks its regional extent; focal subchondral edema lacks impact cause or acute line assessment. Lateral/PF cartilage, synovitis and Baker cyst are unmentioned.

Direct final medial meniscal tear and synovitis support positives. Explicit_absence: normal ACL/MCL/lateral meniscus. Missing_evidence: global cartilage wear worse medially lacks compartment depth/extent; fluid is ungraded; correctly located Baker cyst has numeric-only size and perifocal edema, neither an explicit moderate/large grade; degenerative subchondral edema lacks impact causation/acute fracture-line assessment. Plicae are not the basis for synovitis positive; the direct diagnosis is.

Definite bucket-handle/root/posterior-horn medial meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: continuous normal-signal MCL, no lateral meniscal pathology and normal bone morphology/signal. Below_threshold: continuous mucoid ACL and minimal fluid. Missing_evidence: medial/lateral/trochlear thinning and bare patellar gradeII lack depth/extent; numeric-only 29x13-mm popliteal cyst lacks severity grade. PCL possible partial rupture and LCL chronic findings do not change ACL/MCL targets. Synovitis is unmentioned.

Explicit_absence: normal collateral morphology/signal and remaining bone morphology/signal. Below_threshold: ACL signal increase/distension without a described discontinuity, lateral meniscal degeneration without tear features, small fluid and explicitly small Baker cyst. Missing_evidence: suspected medial horizontal rupture remains equivocal; intercondylar extension is not an independently definite displaced fragment. Unnamed cartilage grades II/III do not map depth/extent. Synovitis is unmentioned.

Explicit_absence/below_threshold: no significant collateral abnormalities for a high-grade target, normal lateral meniscus and other femorotibial/trochlear cartilage, explicitly superficial patellar chondropathy and mild effusion. Missing_evidence: ACL thinning/signal with requested stability correlation lacks current high-grade or preserved-fiber assessment; medial marginal fraying is not a direct tear; partial-depth medial ulcers and unnamed final grade2 lack precise depth/extent. Definite trabecular/cortical fractures with edema are described but without acute timing; associated suspected capsular injury does not date them. Fracture-associated edema does not separately establish a contusion. Synovitis and Baker cyst unmentioned; popliteal edema is not a cyst.

Explicit_absence: normal ACL/collateral ligaments and no meniscal tears. Missing_evidence: no definite bone marrow edema/bony destruction is a qualified exclusion, retained uncertain for contusion/fracture. General no significant abnormal finding does not fill unmentioned cartilage, effusion, synovitis or Baker targets.

Definite medial horizontal meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: normal ACL/MCL/lateral meniscus and preserved femorotibial cartilage. Below_threshold: minor fluid. Missing_evidence: focal patellar ridge degeneration lacks cartilage depth/extent; mild underlying osseous change does not establish impact cause or acute line. Synovitis and Baker cyst are unmentioned.

Direct complete ACL tear, both meniscal tears and named osseous contusions support positives. Below_threshold: mild MCL sprain and minimal fluid. Explicit_absence: intact PF joint. Missing_evidence: medial cartilage thinning lacks depth/extent; mild synovial thickening lacks inflammatory diagnosis; described contusions do not separately exclude a discrete acute fracture line. Lateral cartilage and Baker cyst are unmentioned. Corrupt popliteus muscle-fluid measurement is neither Baker cyst nor cartilage extent.

Direct complex tears of both menisci support positives; likely qualifies their degenerative cause, not the tears. Moderate effusion positive. Below_threshold: continuous degenerative ACL. Missing_evidence: meniscofemoral/deep MCL-layer rupture and distension lack overall high-grade fraction plus acute edema; medial erosion, mild lateral OA and unnamed PF gradeII lack depth/extent; saddle-shaped numeric-only 6.5-cm popliteal cyst lacks severity grade; marrow edema lacks impact cause/acute line assessment. Synovitis unmentioned; plica and popliteus bursitis are distinct.

Explicit_absence: normal collaterals and no lateral meniscal tear. Missing_evidence: suspected ACL gradeII lacks a definite high-grade fraction; irregular medial meniscal surface with injury not excluded is equivocal; focal femoral marrow edema lacks impact causation; qualified tibial/fibular cortical exclusion is neither unqualified nor whole-knee acute-fracture exclusion. All cartilage, effusion, synovitis and Baker targets are unmentioned.

PF positive uses explicit full-thickness ulcers with diffuse patellar distribution (also diffuse extent in conclusion), a qualitative regional-extent inference flagged for review. Explicit_absence: normal cruciates/collaterals. Below_threshold: both menisci have central nonsurfacing signal without tear features; mild fluid. Missing_evidence: femorotibial partial-thickness ulcers and bare final grade2 lack exact depth/extent; leaking popliteal cyst lacks size grade; no significant marrow abnormality is qualified and secondary patellar bone changes do not establish impact/acute fracture. Fat-pad edema does not establish synovitis.

Correspondence flag: source explicitly distinguishes RIGHT-injury indication from the requested/performed LEFT MRI; all current findings and interpretation consistently describe LEFT, so history alone does not mask this internally resolved report. No metadata was consulted. Explicit_absence: intact ligaments/menisci/PF cartilage, no fluid and normal popliteal fossa. Below_threshold: explicitly tiny focus of severe lateral chondrosis is qualitative sub-centimeter-extent inference, flagged for review. Missing_evidence: medial mild thinning lacks depth; nonaggressive focal marrow lesion lacks an explicit whole-knee contusion/fracture assessment. Its 1.5-cm size is not cartilage-loss extent. Synovitis unmentioned.

Direct complete acute ACL rupture, displaced complex lateral meniscal tear and recent pivot-shift osseous contusions support positives. Explicit_absence: normal medial meniscus, no cartilage defects or Baker cyst. Below_threshold: grade-I MCL sprain and small fluid. Missing_evidence: synovial proliferation alone lacks inflammation; normal background marrow around described contusions does not explicitly exclude a discrete fracture line. LCL gradeII does not alter MCL state; parameniscal cyst is not Baker cyst.

Direct medial meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: normal MCL/lateral meniscus/all cartilage, no fluid/Baker cyst. Missing_evidence: chronic ACL tear is not specified as complete or high-grade; chronicity itself is not an exclusion. Synovitis and bone injury targets are not mentioned.

Direct medial meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: normal MCL/lateral meniscus and no Baker cyst. Below_threshold: ACL mucoid degeneration without disruption. Missing_evidence: all-compartment chondromalacia lacks depth/extent. Effusion, synovitis and bone injury are unmentioned. Source-quality flag: literal Test report appears in Results; preserve source and extraction without assuming a fabricated clinical finding or silently discarding it.

Direct lateral femoral bone bruise supports contusion positive; probable previous patellar subluxation qualifies its proposed mechanism rather than the directly described bruise. Explicit_absence: no medial meniscal tear/chondrosis. Below_threshold: grade-I MCL sprain and minimal fluid. Missing_evidence: interstitial ACL tear lacks high-grade fraction; lateral radial tear is suspected; full-depth lateral cartilage fracture has corrupt size tokens and cannot establish extent; patellar subchondral fracture lacks acute timing. Neither intact8 nor loose-fragment intact6 sizes are reconstructed. PF subchondral bone injury is not itself an informative PF cartilage-loss description, so PF OA remains unmentioned, as do synovitis/Baker.

Direct full-depth radial medial meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: intact ACL and lateral meniscus. Below_threshold: low-grade MCL sprain and no significant effusion. Missing_evidence: medial/PF full/high-grade loss lacks extent; relatively well-maintained lateral cartilage is qualified without a depth assessment; stress bone changes do not establish contusion and no sinister marrow changes do not exclude an acute fracture line. Tiny loose-body dimensions are not cartilage-loss extent. Synovitis/Baker unmentioned.

Explicit_absence: intact cruciates/collaterals, normal all cartilage compartments and no fluid. Missing_evidence: small marrow edema possibly stress reaction lacks impact cause/acute fracture assessment. Edema at the lateral meniscal root is osseous localization, not an assessment of meniscal integrity, so both menisci remain unmentioned. Synovitis and Baker cyst unmentioned.

Direct high-grade ACL partial rupture and surfacing medial meniscal tear support positives. Below_threshold: MCL sprain described only as mild proximal signal increase without fiber disruption; flag source severity scope. Minimal fluid below threshold. Explicit_absence: unremarkable PF cartilage. Missing_evidence: no definite lateral tear and no definite fracture line are qualified exclusions. Medial/lateral cartilage, synovitis, Baker cyst and bone-contusion status are not described; anterior subcutaneous edema is not marrow edema.

Direct synovitis supports positive. Explicit_absence: normal collateral ligaments. Below_threshold: ACL grade-I signal-only injury and medial meniscal grade-II internal degeneration. Missing_evidence: global cartilage wear, lateral tibial signal and unnamed severe PF grade4 lack specified qualifying depth/extent; effusion and characteristic-location Baker cyst lack size grades; degenerative subchondral edema lacks impact cause/acute line assessment. Lateral meniscus is unmentioned.

Explicit_absence: normal continuous MCL, no medial meniscal rupture, no significant fluid/Baker cyst and normal bone signal for contusion. Below_threshold: continuous degenerative ACL and medial internal degeneration. Missing_evidence: possible prior lateral root partial tear versus global no rupture leaves current root state unresolved; thinning/unnamed cartilage grades lack depth/extent; tibial fragment is only tentatively a nonunited apophysis, so acute fracture cannot be settled from the initial general normal-morphology sentence. Synovitis is unmentioned; 10-mm fragment is not cartilage-loss extent.

Direct complex flap medial meniscal tear supports positive. Medial OA positive uses explicit full-thickness long-segment disease with nearly completely depleted femorotibial cartilage: qualitative extent flagged. Explicit_absence/below_threshold: intact normal-signal ACL and lateral meniscal mucoid degeneration without tear. Missing_evidence: lateral marginal osteophytes do not state cartilage depth/extent; deep focal PF defects lack size; fluid lacks amount; fat-isointense synovial proliferations do not explicitly establish inflammatory synovitis. MCL, Baker cyst and osseous injury targets are not assessed. Calcified 11-mm loose body is not cartilage-loss measurement.

Direct complex medial meniscal tear and synovitis support positives. Explicit_absence/below_threshold: preserved ACL, grade-I MCL signal-only sprain, lateral degeneration without tear and no Baker cyst. Missing_evidence: severe OA plus unnamed gradesIII/IV lack explicit depth mapping/qualifying regional extent; fluid is ungraded; degenerative subchondral edema/cysts do not establish traumatic contusion or acute fracture. Lateral grade-II sprain is not MCL evidence.

Direct complex surfacing tears of both menisci support positives. Explicit_absence/below_threshold: preserved cruciates and collaterals apart from MCL deep edema without described fiber loss; small increase in fluid. MCL negative uses the explicit otherwise-preserved statement, not edema alone. Missing_evidence: medial/PF loss exceeds 50% but focal region size is absent; subchondral fibrovascular change does not assess traumatic contusion or acute fracture. Millimetric osteophyte/parameniscal-cyst sizes are not cartilage-loss extent. Lateral cartilage, synovitis and Baker cyst are unmentioned; proximal tibiofibular ganglia are separate.

Direct surfacing horizontal medial meniscal tear supports positive. Explicit_absence: normal cruciate/collateral ligaments, normal lateral meniscus, no increased fluid and normal bone signal for contusion. Missing_evidence: normal signal alone does not explicitly exclude an acute cortical fracture line. Cartilage, synovitis and Baker cyst are unmentioned.

notes: Personally read all 50 original gold-blinded reports in five groups of ten and reasoned all 600 targets under frozen rubric. No other 063 annotations, gold, legacy/external labels, regex/NLI labeling or default filling accessed/used. Python only assembled explicit personal choices and validated exact contiguous original-language quotes, schema and UID coverage through rsna.labels.read_reviews. Unfinished work stayed outside initiative. Explicit absence and below-threshold findings distinguished in notes; missing severity/extent/acuity/anatomy and contradictions masked. Only completion/coverage/hashes shared with root; flags withheld pending independent source-first review. Draft does not confer training eligibility or image diagnostic accuracy.
